gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a home backup set charged only from the grid (BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K battery + Apex 300 Home Backup Kit, 5,529.6 Wh, 3,840 W) can go in one store cart as a single bundle SKU for $3,199. That is $98 less than the three parts bought separately ($3,297), compared with ChatGPT's $12,000–$18,000 installed Powerwall estimate. BLUETTI's own page says the Apex 300 'is expected to ship in late January'.
standout_why: I opened the cited West Electric comparison (westelectric.energy/batteries/compare-batteries). It covers only installer-fitted Powerwall 3, Enphase IQ 5P and FranklinWH aPower 2, with installed prices ($9,000–$26,000 in CT). It does not mention BLUETTI, Anker SOLIX or EcoFlow, or any online battery-plus-panel bundle. I did not open the cited Tesla support pages or the FranklinWH manual this run. From their titles and from ChatGPT's answer, they cover Powerwall and aPower behavior, not retail carts. ChatGPT's own cost table gives installed estimates only. No rival gives a single-cart retail kit, its bundle discount or its January ship date. I scored this 2, not 3, because 5.5 kWh and 3,840 W are well below one Powerwall 3 (13.5 kWh, 11.5 kW). The kit is a cheaper way to back up part of a house, not a like-for-like whole-house setup.
kit_items: Battery/inverter: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W). BLUETTI's page says it powers 120 V and 240 V devices at the same time, has a 0 ms UPS switchover and takes up to 11.5 kW of generator input. Because it charges from the grid or a generator, it works without solar.
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K for Apex 300/200 (2,764.8 Wh). It doubles storage to 5,529.6 Wh. Buy the 'for Apex 300/200' listing, not the AC200L/AC300 or AC500 versions.

Home connection: BLUETTI Apex 300 Home Integration Kit, 'Single Apex 300' variant. BLUETTI describes it as the part that 'integrate[s] the power station to home circuit to keep vital home loads powered when the grid goes down.' The 'Parallel' variant ($799) is for two or more Apex 300 units.
